# nuxt-backend-ship: the API

The public names of provider setup, tests, deploying, production checks, monitoring, flags and kill switches, webhooks and rate limits, each with the first sentence of its doc comment.

The file ships inside the package, so it describes exactly the version in `node_modules`. The
core skill, `nuxt-backend`, lists every public name in its own `references/api.md`.

## Auto-imported composables

| Composable | What it does |
|---|---|
| `useFlag()` | Whether a feature flag is on for whoever is looking: their account, their active workspace and their plan, as `backend/flags.ts` declares the flag and the admin console overrides it. |
| `useFlagAdmin()` | The admin console's Flags tab, as data: every flag with its default and its override, and the change an administrator makes, through `listFlags` and `setFlag` of `backend/flags.ts`. |

## Import paths

### `nuxt-backend/http`

| Export | What it is |
|---|---|
| `registerBackendRoutes()` | Mount every route the backend serves on the app's HTTP router: the auth routes, the billing and email webhooks, the metered AI stream, and the health. |

Types: `RegisterBackendRoutesOptions`.

### `nuxt-backend/rate-limit`

| Export | What it is |
|---|---|
| `DEFAULT_LIMITS` | The package's default rate limits — `emailOtp`, `emailOtpGlobal`, `emailOtpAttempt`, `emailChange`, `billingSync`, `ai`, `aiBudget`, `aiGlobal`, `admin`, `invitation`, `invitationGlobal`, `workspaceCreate`, `accountDelete`, `passkeySignIn`, `passkeySignInGlobal`, `signUpOtpGlobal`, `inviteCheck`, `inviteCheckGlobal`, `waitlistJoin`, `waitlistJoinGlobal`, `contact`, `contactGlobal`, `inboundMail`, `inboundMailGlobal`, `report`, `reportGlobal`, `write` and `upload` — guarding the flows the package itself drives. |
| `setupRateLimiter()` | Configure the Rate Limiter component, pre-seeded with `DEFAULT_LIMITS`. |
| `DAY` | Re-exported from `@convex-dev/rate-limiter`. |
| `HOUR` | Re-exported from `@convex-dev/rate-limiter`. |
| `MINUTE` | Re-exported from `@convex-dev/rate-limiter`. |
| `SECOND` | Re-exported from `@convex-dev/rate-limiter`. |

Types: `RateLimiterComponents`, `RateLimitConfig`.

### `nuxt-backend/monitoring`

| Export | What it is |
|---|---|
| `isReportable()` | Whether a failure is worth a report: a crash or an app's own error (no catalog code), or a service that cannot serve the call (`unavailable`). |
| `MONITORING_TAGS` | The tags an event about a backend call carries. |
| `reportError()` | Report an error to the monitoring service, from an action. |
| `checkIn()` | Check a scheduled job in to its monitor, from an action: the job named `send weekly digest` checks in to `send-weekly-digest`. |
| `reportingErrors()` | An action handler that reports what it throws (`reportError`), then rethrows it: the caller still sees the failure. |
| `checkingIn()` | An action handler that checks its job in each time it runs: `ok` with how long the run took, or `error` (with the error reported, then rethrown) when it throws. |

Types: `BackendCronSchedule`, `CheckInStatus`, `CronInterval`, `ReportErrorOptions`, `CheckInOptions`.

### `nuxt-backend/flags`

| Export | What it is |
|---|---|
| `setupFlags()` | Feature flags, evaluated inside your own queries and mutations, and the package's kill switches. |
| `BACKEND_FLAGS` | The package's own flags, which the package itself honors: three kill switches and the maintenance banner. |
| `defineFlags()` | Declare the app's flags: each key with its default and what it turns on. |
| `FLAG_TARGETS_MAX` | The most ids (or plan keys) one target list of an override names. |
| `flagBucket()` | A subject's bucket for a flag, from 0 to `ROLLOUT_BUCKETS` − 1: a 32-bit FNV-1a hash of the flag's key and the subject's id, mixed by MurmurHash3's finalizer. |
| `MAINTENANCE_MESSAGE_MAX` | The longest maintenance message, in characters. |
| `ROLLOUT_BUCKETS` | How finely a rollout is cut: a subject's bucket is one of this many, so a rollout takes hundredths of a percent. |

Types: `FlagValues`, `ExperimentVariantResult`, `ExperimentResult`, `AdminFlag`, `FlagsApi`, `FlagCtx`, `FlagWriteCtx`, `Flags`, `SetupFlagsOptions`, `FlagsComponents`, `ExperimentVerdict`, `RateInterval`, `BackendFlag`, `FlagDefinition`, `FlagDefinitions`, `FlagOverride`, `FlagRolloutSubject`, `FlagSubject`, `PausableService`.

### `nuxt-backend/test`

| Export | What it is |
|---|---|
| `register()` | Register the nuxt-backend all-in-one `backend` component with a test Convex instance, the way the app mounts it: under its name, with its real schema (indexes and document validation included), and with its children registered beneath it: the email provider at `<name>/resend`, the package's migrations at `<name>/migrations`, the waitlist's queue and mirror at `<name>/waitlistRank` and `<name>/waitlistMirror`, and the growth funnel's counts at `<name>/funnelCounts` — convex-test resolves a component's own child calls to those paths. |
| `defineBackendTestApp()` | Your app under test: a fresh convex-test instance per call, with the `backend` component and every component the scaffolded `convex.config.ts` mounts (the action cache, aggregate, migrations, persistent text streaming, the billing provider, the rate limiter, the sharded counter, workflows and the workpool) registered under the names it mounts them by, and the Agent and RAG components (`agent`, `rag`) when the app installs them. |
| `seedWorkspace()` | Create a workspace with no members yet, for several `asUser` callers to join: `asUser(t, { workspace: id, workspaceRole: 'admin' })`. |
| `asUser()` | Create an account in the `backend` component's auth tables and return the instance signed in as it, the way a real sign-in leaves it: the account with the role `'user'`, a personal workspace it owns and has active, and the claims a real token carries. |
| `default` | The default export. |

Types: `TestUserOptions`, `TestUser`.

### `nuxt-backend/test-utils`

| Export | What it is |
|---|---|
| `backendTestAliases()` | Vite aliases that put `createBackendMock` under the package's composables and components and the base module's own. |
| `renderEmail()` | Render one of the emails the package sends, as `setupEmail` with the same options would send it, without a deployment: the template in effect (an override in `templates`, else the packaged one) in the shared layout, in `locale` read through `messages`. |
| `backendMockProvides()` | The mock's client and auth state under the base module's keys and its function tree under this package's, for a plain `mount()`: `mountSuspended` copies them from the Nuxt app, where each new mock is provided, but `mount()` starts an app of its own. |
| `createBackendMock()` | A fake backend for an app's component and page tests: the package's composables and components, and the base module's own (`useQuery`, `<Authenticated>`, the page guard, …), read it instead of a deployment once `backendTestAliases` is in the Vitest project. |
| `resetBackendMock()` | Forget every mock: the active one, the signed-out fallback and the session token the auth layer cached. |

Types: `RenderEmailOptions`, `BackendMock`, `BackendMockCall`, `BackendMockInit`, `BackendMockInvitation`, `BackendMockName`, `BackendMockState`, `BackendMockUser`, `BackendMockWorkspace`.

### `nuxt-backend/eslint`

| Export | What it is |
|---|---|
| `BACKEND_ESLINT_RULES` | The rules the preset turns on, at the levels of the plugin's own recommended config. |
| `backendEslint()` | Two flat-config entries: `nuxt-backend:convex` applies the Convex rules to the functions directory (tests excluded), and `nuxt-backend:generated` ignores every `_generated` folder in it. |

Types: `BackendEslintOptions`.

## CLI

### `npx nuxt-backend doctor`

Check the project + deployment configuration.

- `--cwd`: Project directory
- `--json`: Machine-readable output
- `--fix`: Repair what doctor can: restore missing scaffold files, add missing mounts and routes, push env (`env push`), at a terminal make the first administrator, and apply the provider settings the billing findings recommend and turn a webhook endpoint back on, each after you confirm it
- `--yes`: With --fix: apply the provider changes without asking (for a script or CI)
- `--prod`: Check the production deployment: missing email/billing config becomes a failure, its switches and email are read, and its live site is probed
- `--only`: Check only these capabilities, comma-separated: auth, data, jobs, billing, email, notifications, ai, protection, monitoring, flags, analytics, hosting

`--json`: `{ $schema, findings, summary }`, described by https://nuxt-backend.dev/schemas/doctor.json; with `--fix`, the repair's progress goes to stderr.

### `npx nuxt-backend status`

Show each capability's state — live, test, missing or failing — with its providers, unset env and most pressing finding.

- `--cwd`: Project directory
- `--json`: Machine-readable output
- `--prod`: The production deployment's capabilities, under doctor's production posture and its live probes

`--json`: `{ deployment, status, capabilities: [{ name, title, state, reason, providers, missingEnv, findings, top, docsUrl, devtools }], summary }`: `state` is `live`, `test`, `missing` or `failing`, `status` is `ok`, `degraded` or `failing`.

### `npx nuxt-backend env push`

Sync backend env from .env(.local) to the Convex deployment (dev deployments also get AUTH_SECRET/SITE_URL provisioned).

- `--cwd`: Project directory
- `--prod`: Act on the production deployment; never invent values; fail on missing required env
- `--preview`: Act on the preview deployment of this name (empty: the branch the CI build names, as convex deploy does); fills AUTH_SECRET, test-mode email and sandbox billing
- `--defaults`: Write the project env defaults new deployments of this type start with: preview or dev
- `--site-url`: The SITE_URL to write, replacing the one already set (a preview's own origin)
- `--dry-run`: Print the plan without setting anything
- `--force`: Replace values already on the deployment with the local ones: a comma-separated list of names, or every name but BACKEND_ENVIRONMENT when bare (or "all"), which --prod refuses
- `--json`: Machine-readable output

`--json`: `{ deployment, dev, results: [{ name, action, detail, outcome, error }], missingRequired }`: `deployment` names what was written (`dev:<slug>`, `production`, `preview:<name>`, `defaults:<type>`); values never appear.

### `npx nuxt-backend env rotate`

Rotate AUTH_SECRET, EMAIL_WEBHOOK_SECRET or BILLING_WEBHOOK_SECRET with no downtime: the new value beside the old, then the old retired.

- `<name>`: The secret: AUTH_SECRET, EMAIL_WEBHOOK_SECRET or BILLING_WEBHOOK_SECRET
- `--cwd`: Project directory
- `--prod`: Rotate production's secret
- `--dry-run`: Print each step it would take, and change nothing
- `--retire`: AUTH_SECRET: retire the old value now, not after the 30-day window (after a leak)
- `--json`: Print the outcome as one JSON document; progress goes to stderr

`--json`: `{ name, deployment, dryRun, steps: [{ step, outcome, note? }], state, retiresAt? }`: the steps it took and the secret's new state; values never appear.

### `npx nuxt-backend deploy`

Take production from nothing to a passing doctor --prod: link or create the production deployment, push its env, push the backend, sync the billing catalog, register both webhooks, write the app's env into the Vercel project, then run doctor --prod. Safe to run again.

- `--cwd`: Project directory
- `--dry-run`: Print every step it would take, and change nothing
- `--sandbox`: A demo or staging app: set BACKEND_ENVIRONMENT=sandbox instead of production, and sync to the providers' test modes
- `--build`: Run as the host's build command: put the env the first push needs on production (AUTH_SECRET, SITE_URL from the host), then convex deploy builds the app against the backend
- `--json`: Print the outcome as one JSON document; progress goes to stderr

`--json`: `{ dryRun, environment, host, steps: [{ id, capability, title, outcome, detail }], doctor }`: `outcome` is `done`, `unchanged`, `planned`, `skipped` or `failed`, `doctor` is `{ pass, warn, fail, failing }` or null; values never appear.

### `npx nuxt-backend analyze`

Measure the backend's Convex bundle and the Nuxt app's client and server bundles: the largest packages, the share nuxt-backend and your code bring, and the insights that would shrink them. --max-convex, --max-client and --max-server fail a bundle over its budget.

- `--cwd`: Project directory
- `--only`: Measure one half: convex (seconds, no Nuxt build) or nuxt
- `--max-convex`: Fail when the Convex bundle's code, without source maps, is larger (8MB, 500kB)
- `--max-client`: Fail when the Nuxt client bundle is larger
- `--max-server`: Fail when the Nuxt server bundle is larger
- `--json`: Print the report as one JSON document; progress goes to stderr

`--json`: `{ version, ranAt, bundles: [{ id, title, bytes, gzipBytes, sourceMapBytes, parts, packages, shares, insights, notes }], budgets: [{ bundle, flag, limit, bytes, over, grew }], failures: [{ half, message }] }`: `id` is `convex`, `client` or `server`, and `bytes` is the code without source maps; progress goes to stderr.

### `npx nuxt-backend mcp`

Run the developer MCP server for your coding agent over stdio: the project's state, the docs, and the Convex, billing, email and hosting consoles on your own logins; every tool that writes asks you first.

- `--cwd`: Project directory
- `--prod`: Read production: the project, billing, email and hosting tools read it, the data tools read only its logs and insights, and every write is refused

`--json`: none: it speaks MCP on stdin and stdout until the client closes it.

## Doctor findings

`npx nuxt-backend doctor --json` reports these ids, each with a `docsUrl` that explains it.

| Id | Capability | Checks |
|---|---|---|
| `deployment-monitoring-dsn` | monitoring | Deployment MONITORING_DSN |
| `monitoring-app` | monitoring | App error reports |
| `monitoring-source-maps` | monitoring | Source maps |
| `monitoring-backend-exceptions` | monitoring | Backend exception reporting |
| `monitoring-health` | monitoring | Health endpoint |
| `monitoring-usage-alerts` | monitoring | Usage alerts |
| `site-https` | hosting | HTTPS and HSTS |
| `site-csp` | hosting | Content security policy |
| `site-backend-url` | hosting | Backend the site uses |
| `agent-docs` | hosting | Docs for agents |

## Environment

| Name | Capability | Read on | Tier | Without it |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `MONITORING_DSN` | monitoring | deployment | optional | the backend reports nothing: errors in its actions and its cron check-ins go nowhere (the browser and the Nuxt server report on the DSN the app reads, and in dev a local error log stands in) |

## The scaffold's function contract

The composables call these functions by name; keep them exported from the scaffolded files.

- `backend/flags.ts`: `getFlags`, `listFlags`, `setFlag`, `exposeExperiment`
- `backend/webhooks.ts`: `getWebhookDeliveries`, `replayWebhookDelivery`
